title: Contrastive loss with the positive in the denominator
promptMarkdown: One anchor has positive similarity1 and two negative similarities0,−1. Forτ=.5, calculate normalised candidate probabilities, contrastive loss and derivatives with respect to all three similarities. Repeat the loss when all similarities are equal. Explain why omitting the positive from the denominator changes the objective, and give an example of an augmentation that destroys downstream label information.
hintLadder: Subtract the positive scaled score before exponentiating.
A valid normalised candidate probability has a denominator containing its numerator term.
